column7: The bounded require_mfa upgrade grace period (#2923) must not be extendable by setting the system clock back. The grace clock high-water mark (system_metadata adr112.require_mfa.grace_clock) is written at boot and every minute while the period runs; a boot counts from max(now, recorded clock, start) and the running server from max(wall clock, boot floor + monotonic elapsed), so a backward step is ignored and a forward step only ends the grace period sooner. Proving test: day-29 clock recorded, wall clock back at day 2 -> the window floor is day 29 and a WARNING names the backward clock; a recorded clock past the deadline ends the grace period whatever the wall clock says. Red when the boot ignores the recorded clock. Siblings: TestADR112MFAGrace_StartIsDurable (start not reset by a restart), TestADR112MFAGrace_CorruptFactsFailClosed, TestMFAUpgradeGrace_BackwardClockStepDoesNotExtend (core, in-process step; SQLite + Postgres).
